title: Playing in Vicksburg and Natchez; Bud Scott's string band
summary: He lists Vicksburg clubs, and says string bands like Bud Scott's of Natchez were typical there.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Did you ever live in Vicksburg? Oh, yeah.

Long? I played in Vicksburg. At the Princess Theater. I played 1014 Washington Street at Zach Luris' Nightclub. Played down to Steamboat Exchange, down to Fitzgerald, they called it. A lot of places. Yeah. Bells Cafe. How long did you stay?
When you go to a town like that, did you stay?
Well, I stayed in Vicksburg for a couple of years. I used to play at Henderson, Royer Garden, and Fairty, Louisiana.
What kind of bands were up there? Did they sound about the same kind of jazz they played in New Orleans, or?
Well, no, they mostly had string bands all up through there. Bud Scott had the best band around up through there, from Natchez, Mississippi. Then they had a lot of...
Was that the Bud Scott that was with Kidore and went to Chicago?
No, that wasn't the same one. He had a string band, this Bud Scott. Bud Scott also played guitar.

Well, this one he played a mandolin. And he was a wonderful singer. He had a lot of good musicians, but they were string instruments. Mark Hawkins, Forrest Hawkins, Bubba Quirk, Walter, and the gang, you know, they all played the bandolons, guitars, and the first one thing I liked.
It wouldn't have been Little Walters up here at the Harmonic. Not this one, no. You played, you said, in Natchez too, a while? Oh, yeah.
Well, I played in Natchez quite a bit. Different times.
